SMTO-LLM-0055 — SMTO couldn't tell which parts of the model's actions go together

GUID: 377630e2-22a3-4296-addd-2954ddd3dd2a
Slug: streamed-tool-order-ambiguous
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: llm

What happened

  • The model sent its actions in pieces as it typed, without the numbers that show which piece belongs where. SMTO ran none of them rather than piece them together by guesswork.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the steps already shown for this task in the conversation and note which ones finished before the error. Work finished before this reply still stands, so you only need SMTO to continue, not redo it.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and pick a different model for Main (and Helper, if one is set), then save. This mix-up comes from how the model server streams actions; another model or server usually numbers them properly.
  3. If someone else runs your AI model server, tell them streamed tool calls arrive without an index and ask them to update its tool-calling support. Newer server versions and correct tool parsers number every piece so the order is clear.
  4. Send a new message asking SMTO to continue from where it stopped, without repeating the steps that already finished. Guessing the order could change what runs, so a cleanly ordered reply is the safe way forward.

What success looks like

  • SMTO carries out the model's next actions and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your AI model server. Don't ask SMTO to redo steps that already finished.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Streamed tool_calls fragments lack a stable index while more than one call is present (or an implicit-index stream later uses a nonzero index), so no single call order could be established and the stream was rejected before dispatch.

What this means

  • Streamed call fragments lack a stable index or identity from which one deterministic call order can be established. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Streamed call fragments lack a stable index or identity from which one deterministic call order can be established.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare call indexes and identities across provider events; distinguish a harmless repeated fragment from conflicting order information.

How to fix it

  • Fix the serving stack or proxy so every streamed tool_calls delta carries a stable integer index (and call id); missing indexes are usually a tool-parser or proxy bug. Otherwise route to a compatible endpoint in Settings › Setup › Model routing. Do not reorder fragments heuristically.
  • Repair the serving stack’s stable call indexes/identities. Do not reorder ambiguous fragments into executable operations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • All fragments assemble into a stable ordered set of calls without identity or index conflicts.

What not to do

  • Do not replay prior successful operations to repair a later model response.
  • Do not disable protocol validation or treat this representation failure as input-context overflow.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
